title: Bad Trips Guide, Round 61
intro: Round 61 (2026-11-27). Your "a" on round 60 keeps the gut-driven paragraphs as they are. Your answer on the ferments is in, nearly word for word, and the paragraph reads [Human High in one window](https://www.pangram.com/history/cd5a0e49-7df7-451b-9bc3-0728297b1b7b). [Each point and where it went](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/main/articles/bad-trips/review/r60/RESULTS-R60.md).

For the questions you left open, I read [your ZeoCharge post](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/p/here-is-why-everyone-should-use-zeocharge), which the section's heading links. It answers some of them, and card 1 shows what I took from it. Three zeolite paragraphs now read Human High by themselves ([how you take it](https://www.pangram.com/history/fe031537-bb41-4546-9e44-43acdd13df98), [how you ozonate it](https://www.pangram.com/history/e36188fb-6982-4218-a048-6bf30476bc3f), and [the metal paragraph with it](https://www.pangram.com/history/c6363909-7c94-4758-82e9-ecfc47240fef)). The fourth is card 3. Activated Charcoal reads [Human High](https://www.pangram.com/history/ae42aae9-c334-4a8f-a606-2ed5c9d313b9) in my version, but the warning check won't let it in without your word: card 2 ([every check](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/main/articles/bad-trips/humanize/h79-20261126/RESULTS.md); [what is left](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/main/articles/bad-trips/humanize/h79-20261126/LEFT.md)).

suggestions.title: 1. ZeoCharge & Ferment: what I took from your ZeoCharge post, and one dose line I left out
suggestions.whose: the post's paragraphs, drafted by a model from his practice, with facts from his ZeoCharge post
suggestions.question:
Your post answered three of the questions you left open, and these went in (highlighted):
1.1 "a spoonful of zeolite into a cup of water or juice", from your "mix a spoon or 2 of the zeolite into a (non-metal) cup of water ... or juice".
1.2 "however much zeolite was in the water", from your "this works regardless of how much zeolite I am ozonating". Your post says 20 minutes at 1000mg an hour; the guide's ten minutes at two grams an hour is the same amount of ozone, so the guide's numbers stay.
1.3 "Zeolite binds metals, which is part of why it is used for heavy-metal removal, so I don't put it into a metal thing or use a metal spoon", from your "Zeolite binds metals, so don't put it into a metal thing or use a metal spoon."
1.4 "holding its jar in my hand", from your "HOLD the zeolite in your hand".
One line I left out: "If the zeolite dose at 5g makes you feel worse (or only slightly better), you (usually) need to take MORE. But if taking more does make you feel worse, then you might have a bad zeolite!" It answers two of your questions (whether to repeat it, and how to tell a bad zeolite). But in a guide for someone sitting with a friend, it says to give more to a person who feels worse, so I didn't put it in.
Still open: rubbing it on the body, is that the dry powder or the mix in water?
(a) fine as they are, and the 5g line stays out; (b) add the 5g line after the dose sentence; or write the line as you'd say it. And a word on the rubbing, if you like.
suggestions.why: the facts come from your ZeoCharge post but weren't in this guide, and the 5g line is a dosing call only you can make
suggestions.stays: the paragraphs as highlighted, which are in the guide now
suggestions.advice_note: (a): the 5g line would need its "feel worse" explained before a sitter could act on it safely

suggestions.title: 2. Activated Charcoal: may two lines with no caution in them be said in other words?
suggestions.whose: the post's paragraphs, drafted by a model from his practice
suggestions.question:
As your post has it, Activated Charcoal reads [AI, High](https://www.pangram.com/history/73098017-5efb-41ae-9b5f-92560768e5bd). My version keeps every fact and reads [Human High in one window](https://www.pangram.com/history/ae42aae9-c334-4a8f-a606-2ed5c9d313b9):
"I don't treat charcoal and zeolite as interchangeable, because drugs bind to activated charcoal as well as gut toxins, so it can flatten or reduce a trip.
So if someone took too much, or the gut itself is toxic, I give charcoal. If the trip is going fine and only the gut feels bad, I give zeolite, which leaves the trip alone.
Medicines bind to charcoal too, so I'd think twice before giving it to someone who depends on one, and I'd tell any medics who come that charcoal was taken."
It isn't in the guide yet. The check that guards your warnings holds two of the post's lines word for word, because each has a warning word in it ("toxicity" and "stop"): "Activated charcoal can help gut toxicity, but it adsorbs drugs." and "When the goal is to reduce drug absorption or stop a toxic gut situation, charcoal may be relevant." Neither line is a caution. A version that keeps their exact words would have to bring back "may be relevant", which two readers marked as the line's AI hedge.
(a) my version goes in, and from now on a line whose only warning word isn't a caution may be said in other words, as long as every fact stays; (b) my version goes in, this time only; (c) your post's words stay.
suggestions.why: the check's rule is your call: it was set so that no warning gets reworded without you
suggestions.stays: the three paragraphs as your post has them, until you answer
suggestions.advice_note: (a): it would also let the guide's other lines with "stop" or "risk" in a plain sentence be fixed without a card each

suggestions.tested:
My version, from your ZeoCharge post: "I use powdered zeolite rather than nano-liquid zeolite. Many products did nothing for me, I think because most zeolites have clogged pores that haven't been cleaned, but ZeoCharge is sold as cleaned." Its reading changes with whatever sits next to it.

With the paragraph before it: its first sentence High, its second Medium ([check](https://www.pangram.com/history/38bb7235-8994-4644-92bf-a05d500f19b0)).

With the ozone paragraph after it: High for both sentences, but the ozone paragraph's safety line goes Medium ([check](https://www.pangram.com/history/bf5f7b19-a34b-42e8-9158-22e90c45ac1c)).

With the safety line joined to the sentence before: the first sentence Medium, and the whole ozone paragraph Medium ([check](https://www.pangram.com/history/9363878c-76d1-498c-a49d-4388cf31a388)).

Six earlier tries with the paragraph before it, ending in Low and Medium. The ozone paragraph by itself reads [High](https://www.pangram.com/history/e36188fb-6982-4218-a048-6bf30476bc3f).
suggestions.sense: Fresh readers asked of the post's version: what "nano-liquid zeolite" is, how to tell a good product before a trip when sober people feel little, and what "cleaned" means. Your post says ZeoCharge is sold "cleaned and remineralized", but not whether ozonating is what cleans the others.
suggestions.why: Both of its sentences are short, and every way I join them pushes a neighbour below High. How you'd say which zeolite to buy, and why most don't work, would teach me how to write the short connecting paragraphs the guide has between its longer ones.
suggestions.advice_note: Edit it: which zeolite to get and why, in your words. If ozonating is what cleans the pores, saying so here links it to the next paragraph.
